title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee March 17-18, 2026
summary: The March 17-18, 2026 FOMC meeting minutes reveal a committee navigating significant market volatility driven by AI-related business model concerns and a Middle East conflict that pushed crude oil front-month futures up approximately 50%. Policy rate expectations shifted materially higher, with markets now pricing no rate cuts this year and roughly 30% probability of rate hikes through early next year, diverging from the Desk survey's median projection of two 25bp cuts. The committee noted elevated inflation pressures while recognizing the labor market had shown some easing, with PCE inflation at 2.8% in January.
key_points: Front-month crude oil futures rose approximately 50% over the intermeeting period, with longer-dated futures rising significantly less, suggesting market expectations of a relatively short-lived price increase

Near-term fed funds rate path implied by futures shifted higher, with rate cut not fully priced in until December; options modal path now consistent with no rate change this year versus one 25bp cut previously
Probability of rate hikes through early 2027 increased to approximately 30% per options prices, while distribution of outcomes became more dispersed
Desk survey median continued to show two 25bp rate cuts this year, though respondents pushed out timing; market intelligence suggests some shifted to fewer cuts post-survey
One-year inflation swap rate rose nearly 50 basis points over the period, but forward inflation compensation beyond one year was little changed, indicating anchored long-term inflation expectations

Standing repo operations reached $30 billion on one settlement day (third-largest volume since inception), with interdealer repo rates near standing repo rate, suggesting greater willingness to use operations following December changes
Reserves projected to average approximately $3 trillion through September; monthly pace of reserve management purchases likely to be reduced significantly after April
PCE inflation was 2.8% in January 2026; unemployment rate little changed with low job gains
why_it_matters: This FOMC minutes document captures the committee's assessment during a period of acute market stress from an AI-driven equity correction and a Middle East conflict that spiked energy prices. The divergence between market-implied rate expectations and Desk survey projections highlights evolving uncertainty about the policy path. For rate-sensitive assets, the repricing from roughly one cut to no cuts this year represents a material shift in the expected cost of carry. The committee's monitoring of private credit redemption requests and software sector credit stress also signals emerging market vulnerability considerations.
macro_context: The Middle East conflict created a stagflationary shock with oil up 50% and equity down 5%, complicating the Fed's inflation-versus-growth calculus. The one-year inflation swap rate rose 50bp while longer-term breakevens were stable, suggesting markets viewed the inflation shock as temporary but with near-term implications. Several central banks (ECB, BoC, SNB) previously expected to hold or ease are now expected to hike modestly as a result of energy-driven global inflation pressures.
market_structure_context: Treasury market liquidity diminished somewhat with increased yield volatility but continued to function well. Standing repo operations reached $30 billion (third-largest usage) with interdealer repo rates near the standing repo rate, indicating improved willingness to use standing facilities following December framework changes. Reserve management purchases continue with reserves projected at ~$3 trillion through September, though monthly RMP pace expected to moderate after April tax season.
